title: Adjective + Noun Collocations

topic_snapshot.description: Powerful descriptive pairings to enhance clarity and precision in task responses. Expanding vocabulary beyond simple adjectives.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Felt or experienced very strongly or in an extreme way.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: The invention of the smartphone has had a profound impact on how we communicate.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A visual metaphor of a deep impact, like a heavy stone dropped in a calm pond creating massive, far-reaching ripples.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Existing as a natural or basic part of something.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: There are inherent risks associated with extreme sports like BASE jumping.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A DNA strand glowing, symbolizing something that is naturally built-in or intrinsic.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Able to work as intended or able to succeed.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: Solar power is becoming a increasingly viable alternative to fossil fuels.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A thriving, green plant growing out of a lightbulb, representing a successful and workable idea.

collocation_builder.meaning: A very strong and deep effect.
collocation_builder.example: The new policy will have a profound impact on the local economy.

collocation_builder.meaning: A danger that is an unavoidable part of a situation.
collocation_builder.example: Investors must be aware of the inherent risks of cryptocurrency.

collocation_builder.meaning: A practical and effective answer to a problem.
collocation_builder.example: We need to find a viable solution to the city's housing shortage.

collocation_builder.meaning: An essential or necessary component of something.
collocation_builder.example: Technology has become an integral part of modern education.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: A profound impact / A significant influence
upgrade_section.example: Climate change is having a profound impact on global weather patterns.
Wind energy is a viable alternative to traditional power sources.
Teamwork is an integral component of any successful business.

sentence_frames: It is undeniable that [A] has had a profound impact on [B].
One viable alternative to [A] is to implement [B].
Despite the inherent risks, many still choose to...

ielts_usage_examples.writing_example: While transitioning to green energy involves inherent financial risks, it remains the only viable solution to combat global warming.
ielts_usage_examples.speaking_example: Smartphones have become an integral part of our daily routines; they've had a profound impact on how we interact with the world.

common_mistakes: Using 'a strong impact' instead of the more academic 'a profound impact' or 'a significant impact'.
Confusing 'invaluable' (meaning extremely useful) with 'valueless' (meaning having no value). An invaluable asset is a good thing!

quiz.question: Which adjective correctly collocates with 'alternative' to mean 'practical and able to succeed'?
quiz.explanation: A 'viable alternative' is one that can actually work successfully.

quiz.question: What does 'inherent risk' mean?

options.A: A risk that is easily avoided.
options.B: A risk that is a natural and unavoidable part of something.
options.C: A risk that was created by mistake.
options.D: A risk that is extremely dangerous but rare.

quiz.explanation: Inherent means existing as a natural or basic part of something.
